templates.pattern: A man walks into a bar and asks for water. The bartender pulls out a gun. The man says thank you and leaves. Why?
templates.explanation: The man had hiccups. Bartender scared him with gun, curing hiccups. He thanked him and left.

templates.pattern: A woman shoots her husband, drowns him, hangs him, but they go to dinner together. How?
templates.explanation: She is a photographer. She shoots a photo, develops it in water (drowns), hangs photo to dry.

templates.pattern: What has keys but no locks, space but no room, you can enter but can't go inside?
templates.explanation: A keyboard has keys, spacebar, and enter key but none of the physical versions.

templates.pattern: A man pushes his car to a hotel and tells the owner he is bankrupt. Why?
templates.explanation: He is playing Monopoly. Landed on hotel property and cannot pay rent.

templates.pattern: What gets wetter as it dries?
templates.explanation: A towel gets wetter as it dries you off.

templates.pattern: Romeo and Juliet are found dead on the floor with water and broken glass around them. What happened?
templates.explanation: Romeo and Juliet are fish. Their glass bowl broke and they died.

templates.pattern: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What is it?
templates.explanation: Footsteps. The more steps you take, the more footprints you leave behind.

templates.pattern: A man dies of thirst in his own home. Why?
templates.explanation: Power was out and pipes were frozen. He could not access water despite being home.

templates.pattern: What can travel around the world while staying in a corner?
templates.explanation: A postage stamp stays in the corner of an envelope but travels worldwide.

templates.pattern: A man lives on 15th floor. Every day takes elevator down. Going up, stops at 7th and walks rest. Why?
templates.explanation: He is too short to reach the button above 7th floor. Walks the remaining floors.

templates.pattern: What has a head and tail but no body?
templates.explanation: A coin has a heads side and a tails side but no body.

templates.pattern: Man says: Brothers and sisters I have none, but that man's father is my father's son. Who is in the painting?
templates.explanation: My father's son = me. That man's father = me. So the painting shows his own son.

templates.pattern: Forward I am heavy, backward I am not. What am I?
templates.explanation: The word TON forward is a unit of weight. Backward it spells NOT which is not heavy.

templates.pattern: A doctor and boy are fishing. Boy is doctor's son but doctor is not boy's father. How?
templates.explanation: The doctor is the boy's mother. A common lateral thinking puzzle about gender assumptions.

templates.pattern: What breaks when you say it?
templates.explanation: Silence breaks the moment you speak.

templates.pattern: Man in all black walks dark street. Car with no lights comes but stops in time. How did driver see him?
templates.explanation: It was daytime. A dark street does not necessarily mean nighttime.

templates.pattern: What belongs to you but others use it more than you do?
templates.explanation: Your name belongs to you, but other people say and use it more than you do.

templates.pattern: A man is found dead in a phone booth with stab wounds. No weapon found. What happened?
templates.explanation: He was stabbed with an icicle which melted afterward, leaving only a water puddle.

templates.pattern: What can run but never walks, has a mouth but never talks, has a bed but never sleeps?
templates.explanation: A river runs, has a mouth where it meets the ocean, and has a riverbed.

templates.pattern: Two fathers and two sons go fishing. They catch 3 fish, one each. How is that possible?
templates.explanation: Grandfather, father, and son = 3 people. Grandfather and father are 2 fathers. Father and son are 2 sons.

templates.pattern: What gets bigger the more you take away from it?
templates.explanation: A hole gets bigger as you remove more material from it.

templates.pattern: A man goes out in heavy rain with no protection but not a single hair gets wet. How?
templates.explanation: He has no hair at all. So no hair can get wet.

templates.pattern: What has 13 hearts but no other organs?
templates.explanation: A standard deck of cards has 13 hearts (the suit): Ace through King.

templates.pattern: A woman gave birth to two sons on same hour, same day, same year but they are not twins. How?
templates.explanation: They are part of triplets or more. Not twins but born at the same time.

templates.pattern: What occurs once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
templates.explanation: The letter M appears once in minute, twice in moment, and zero times in thousand years.
